name: Coral bleaching
summary: NOAA has not declared a fifth global bleaching event as of 28 Nov; El Niño keeps the risk of one elevated
state: NOAA Coral Reef Watch says the fourth global bleaching event, which hit about 84% of reef area, likely ended in 2025, and its status page, last updated on 2 Jun 2026, declares no fifth event (NOAA). Scientists told Reuters in late August that another bleaching event was very likely in 2026 as El Niño intensified (bdnews24, 31 Aug). Searches on 28 Nov found no new NOAA global declaration, so Normal holds, with risk rising into the southern summer.
for_you: Reef-dependent fisheries and tourism, especially in the Pacific, Indian Ocean and Australia, are most exposed if bleaching spreads during the southern summer.
rubric_hit: Normal: NOAA declares no global bleaching event in progress (status page as of 28 Nov)

sources.title: NOAA Coral Reef Watch — Current global bleaching: status update
bdnews24 (Reuters) — Coral bleaching occurring too frequently for reefs to recover, scientists say

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
